updates.summary: A count of spells cast is tested `>= 1`, as every other event history count is.
updates.evidence: In the allowed population of the pinned export, every other event history count tested for at least one occurrence uses `>= 1` (83 of them count spells cast). These five Spell Cast tests alone use `> 0`. Patrician's Scorn, Soul Reap and Talara's Battalion read Dream Thief's wording, "if you've cast another <color> spell this turn", with `>= 1`.

changes.face: I Bask in Your Silent Awe

updates.summary: One explicitly defined X is captured once before drawing and losing life, including kinded counter counts.
updates.evidence: Bone Devourer says "you draw X cards and you lose X life, where X is the number of +1/+1 counters on it". Necropotence Avatar says "put a death counter on Necropotence Avatar. You draw X cards and you lose X life, where X is the number of death counters on Necropotence Avatar". Both uses name the same defined quantity; the latter definition is evaluated after counter placement. The pinned reference already uses BindValue followed by two BoundValue reads for Parting Thoughts (all counters on the destroyed target) and Savanti Romero, Time's Exile (all counters on the source after counter placement). These two kinded counts use duplicate inline CountCounters operands. Normalize them to that existing shared-X form; retain the reference's object identity (EventSubject for Bone Devourer, Source for Necropotence Avatar), counter kind, CurrentOrLastKnown, the preceding placement and original action result IDs. No source/holder alias, AST schema change or equality exception is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Suspect uses KeywordEach for singleton objects and optional target populations, as it already does for sets.
updates.evidence: The allowed pinned export has 13 scalar Keyword{action:Suspect{object}} operations and seven KeywordEach{action:Suspect,objects} operations for the same keyword action. Barbed Servitor, Frantic Scapegoat and Person of Interest already suspect one object with KeywordEach; Convenient Target and Incriminating Impetus do so for the attached creature. The scalar form is the same action on One(object), with its actor unchanged. An up-to-one target denotes its entire announced Targets(slot) population, including zero objects, rather than selecting index zero. Preserve Source, EventSubject, moved-object Result references, target slots and all result identities. The owned canonical contract normalizes the same forms for edited/synthesized IR and preserves their typed ID provenance. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: An explicit look-at-top-X definition is captured once for later selections or comparisons, as on Keldon Flamesage.
updates.evidence: Emergent Woodwurm says "look at the top X cards of your library, where X is its power" and then permits a permanent card "with mana value X or less". Its own and Backup-granted attack triggers share one definition in their respective ability-holder scopes. Kiora, Sovereign of the Deep says X is the triggering spell's mana value and permits a spell with mana value less than X. Thassa's Oracle defines X as devotion before looking and reordering, then compares that same X to the remaining library count. The pinned reference repeats ObjectProperty or CountManaSymbols at these later uses, while Keldon Flamesage already uses one BindValue and two BoundValue reads for the analogous look and mana-value selection. Normalize these four programs to one capture immediately before LookAt; preserve each original definition (EventSubject, property, information policy or devotion population), all original action/result IDs, Group structure, optional choices and reordering/cast operands. Allocate only a fresh definition result. The library-count operand of Thassa's later comparison remains live, evaluated after reordering. No Source/holder alias, global live-value equivalence, AST schema change or scorer exception is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: A current battlefield Zone population does not repeat its own InZone(Battlefield) filter.
updates.evidence: Audit of the immutable allowed population found 22 sites on 22 faces with Matching{objects:Zone{scope:Shared(Battlefield),...},filter:InZone(Shared(Battlefield))}. The inner population consists only of current battlefield objects, so that outer membership test cannot remove an object. Other battlefield counts already use the Zone directly. ED-E, Lonesome Eyebot exposes both forms for the same "number of attacking creatures" wording once shared scalar comparisons are supported. Preserve the complete inner Zone subtree, including its kind, object filters, player/object references and binding IDs. Remove only the exact repeated Shared(Battlefield) membership test; do not simplify historical/observed sets, other zones, different filters or unknown operands. This normalization is owned by oracle-ir-contract and retains mapped ID origins. Native validation continues to reject extra fields. No information-policy, timing, holder, result-identity or AST schema change is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Limited Resources makes every player sacrifice their unselected lands, after all players have chosen.
updates.evidence: The Oracle entry trigger says "each player chooses five lands they control and sacrifices the rest". The pinned IR collects each player's choices with ForEachPlayer(All), but the following Sacrifice names only One(AbilityController). The sacrifice must act for All players, using the existing aggregate Unselected choice receipt. Preserve the two-instruction structure: all players choose before the sacrifice operation; do not move sacrifices inside the per-player choice loop. Only the sacrifice actor changes. The choice populations, controller filters, counts, result IDs and trigger subject remain unchanged. The owned AST already supports PlayerSet::All, so schema 190 remains unchanged. A regression checks the action order, aggregate receipt, actor set and printing an edited keep count. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: An immediate sole-use capture and a pure Snapshot pump share the inline value form.
updates.evidence: Audit of the immutable allowed population found 10 faces that bind one deterministic scalar immediately before a Snapshot pump and use the result only in its power/toughness operands. Snapshot evaluates values as that instruction resolves; without an intervening action or another consumer, these captures have the same value and timing as inline expressions. Charix preserves the negative toughness operand; Raffine's Silencer preserves both negative operands and CurrentOrLastKnown information. Gloom Ripper and Monoist Circuit-Feeder are excluded because a second continuous effect also uses their captured values; Myr Battlesphere is excluded because its later damage reuses the captured quantity. Other reference pumps already inline the same kinds of counts/properties. Preserve every source, affected population, player/target identity, duration, remaining result ID, and complete expression subtree. Owned canonicalization checks every typed ResultId use, rejects nonlocal Affected/free Candidate references and unknown fields, and only handles pure single-change Snapshot pumps. It does not move captures across actions or normalize live evaluation, random/choice-dependent values, descendant Ability scopes, or expressions with result references. No lowering correction, information-policy change or AST schema change is introduced. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Phyrexian Ingester sums the current power and toughness of all linked creature cards in exile.
updates.evidence: The printed static ability defines X and Y using the same linked exiled creature-card population. The official Commander Masters release notes state that the bonuses use current power/toughness in exile, update when those values change, and give no bonus for a card that is not a creature in exile (https://magic.wizards.com/en/news/feature/commander-masters-release-notes). CR 607.3 requires summing variable answers when the linked exile ability has exiled multiple cards, such as from copied triggers (https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260619.pdf). The old power operand chooses Query index zero from an unordered unfiltered linked population and cannot represent multiple linked cards; toughness uses a separate implicit Earlier(Exiled) measure. Replace both with Aggregate(Sum) over Zone(Shared(Exile),Card,AllOf(ExiledWith(Source),CardType(Creature))). Preserve the complete triggered exile ability, holder/source, affected object and static evaluation. This is an IR lowering/reference correction, not an equality alias: a first member and a whole population remain distinct. Existing AST types support the correction; no schema, model pin or reference lock change. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Creeping Inn counts creature cards among its linked exiled cards.
updates.evidence: The immutable allowed Oracle text explicitly defines X as the number of creature cards exiled with this creature. The seeded reference definition counts every linked card without a Creature predicate. Add CardType(Creature) to that same live Exile/Card population. Keep the complete payment, its strict movement selection and player, the conditional payment receipt, the BindValue capture after successful payment and before either life amount, both bound uses, and the independent phasing ability unchanged. This corrects an omitted written predicate; it is not an equality alias between filtered and unfiltered populations. Existing AST types support the corrected CountObjects filter. No model pin, reference lock or AST schema change. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: A current all-player zone filtered to the ability controller's same zone uses that player scope directly.
updates.evidence: Audit of the immutable allowed reference found 495 exact current ObjectSet::Zone sites on 424 faces with Players(All) and either InZone(Players(One(AbilityController))) alone or exactly one same-zone membership term in AllOf. Intersecting all players' current instances of a zone with the controller's instance selects precisely that controller's zone. Move the intact One(AbilityController) scope into Zone and remove only that redundant InZone term. Preserve the zone name, object kind, every remaining filter and all containing operations, quantities, identities, histories and capture timing. Other same-zone membership clauses, different controllers, other player expressions, unknown fields and other selector types are excluded. The existing owned oracle-ir-contract canonical::narrow_zone_scope already defines this equality; no new alias, AST schema, model pin, reference lock, grammar rule or compiler rebuild is required. Old source operands are retained and validated through the native canonicalizer. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: High Tide and Bubbling Muck give bonus mana to the player who tapped the land.
updates.evidence: The immutable allowed Oracle text says: Until end of turn, whenever a player taps an Island/a Swamp for mana, that player adds an additional mana of the named color. The CreateTrigger event records TapsForMana with players All. That player therefore refers to this event’s tapping player (PlayerRef::EventSubject), not to the controller of the spell or its delayed triggered ability (PlayerRef::AbilityController). The seeded m_until_end_of_turn_event_clause_that_player hardcoded the latter. Replace only the AddMana player leaf; preserve the delayed event, its filter, duration, announcement, results, mana color and quantity. The shared scoped trigger grammar already binds the written player correctly. Existing AST types suffice; no schema, model pin or reference lock change. This is a semantic correction, not a canonicalization alias between the two player identities. See docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Yurlok’s unobserved fixed universal mana action uses one AddMana(All) instruction.
updates.evidence: The allowed immutable Oracle text says Each player adds {B}{R}{G}. Native Instruction::ForEachPlayer specifies simultaneous actions after APNAP choices (CR 101.4). This body has only one unrestricted fixed literal mana production, with its recipient exactly the loop-bound player and no choice, dynamic amount, ordering directive or result observer. It has the same meaning as one AddMana with players All and the unchanged complete mana bundle. The owned canonicalizer now proves this narrow reduction using bounded typed lossless matching, lexical binding and whole-ability result-use checks, including future programs. It preserves the moved child effect’s result and provenance, and rejects invalid duplicate bindings, extra operands and forged origin metadata. Replace the loop instruction with its child AddMana addressing All; preserve all other abilities, costs, filters, quantities and result identities. Both native forms validate and canonicalize to the same meaning; this is not an alias for arbitrary player loops, choice-bearing or dynamic mana, restrictions, ordering or observed receipts. No AST type/schema, model pin or reference-lock change. See SPEC.md and docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Positive fixed literal mana in one production uses canonical totals by color.
updates.evidence: ManaProduction::All explicitly describes one production, not independent productions. A bundle containing only positive Constant amounts of White, Blue, Black, Red, Green or Colorless mana has the same colors and total units whether represented by repeated units, nested literal All bundles or one amount per color. The owned canonicalizer now merges these pure literal totals with checked i64 arithmetic and a fixed color order. Zero amounts, chosen colors, choices, dynamic expressions, empty bundles, overflow and unknown fields are excluded. This bounded typed normalization preserves all recipients, instructions, restrictions, receipt IDs and their observers, as well as every nonliteral production. The recursive literal-mana grammar’s inverse removes one current unit at a time and enumerates every available first color, preserving exact keyed orders without relying on saved wording. Change only schema-typed ManaProduction roots identified through the owned frozen schema 190; do not inspect or rewrite opaque metadata. Each replacement includes only literal-bundle normalization inside that same production. Existing AST types suffice; no schema, model pin or reference-lock change. See SPEC.md and docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Alternative casting restrictions use one CastSpell predicate with alternative object filters.
updates.evidence: The Ringhart Crest says "cast a creature spell of the chosen type or a legendary creature spell". Its pinned reference uses ManaUse::Either of two CastSpell predicates; Volshe Tideturner expresses "cast an instant or sorcery spell or a kicked spell" as one CastSpell with ObjectFilter::AnyOf. Both test the same payment action against alternative spell filters. Normalize only nonempty Either nodes whose every arm is exactly CastSpell. Preserve every entire filter and all typed references, including source, chosen type and target identity. The owned typed canonicalizer performs the same reduction after visiting children, without revisiting or renumbering their IDs. Other payment actions, mixed alternatives, conjunctions, negation, source-domain flags, conditions, spending changes and invalid extra fields are not merged. The complete allowed pinned reference was scanned only at schema-190 ManaUse sites, with opaque metadata excluded; this is the sole matching face. Existing AST types suffice; no model schema, pin or reference-lock change. This is equivalent-shape normalization, not a semantic correction. See SPEC.md and docs/grammar-simplification-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Damage-prevention shields preserve the written damage source and recipient direction.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #4 reports nine reversed prevention events in pinned schema-190 records. Balduvian Hydra, Ethereal Champion, Opal-Eye Konda's Yojimbo, Ordruun Commando, Rasputin Dreamweaver, Revered Elder, Rock Hydra and Ursine Fylgja prevent damage dealt TO the named creature; retain arbitrary damage sources and match that creature as recipient. Barbed Wire instead prevents damage dealt BY that artifact; restrict the source to that same permanent and allow every recipient. Preserve the amount, duration, limit, event kind/grouping/subject, costs, controller and replacement body. The current grammar's seeded meanings contain the same reversal and are corrected alongside these records; this is a semantic correction, not an equality normalization. Existing AST types suffice. Issue: https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/4 . Upstream repair evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/91a2fe43 . The local regression family checks each corrected native event and rejects the old readings. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Gauntlets of Chaos destroys only attached Auras after its successful exchange.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #5: the Oracle sentence says destroy all Auras attached to the exchanged permanents. The reference matches either attachment target but omits Subtype(Aura), so attached Equipment is incorrectly included. Conjoin the existing complete attachment disjunction with the Aura subtype, preserving both target slots, the exchange-success guard, cost, ordering and destruction regeneration flag. Do not replace the disjunction or widen the subtype test. This corrects one typed filter operand and the matching seeded grammar declaration; no AST schema change or equality alias. Upstream repair evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/855deccc . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/5 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Mercenaries prevention matches damage from that creature to the activating player.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #6: the next-time shield names both this creature and you. The reference retains AbilityController as recipient but has Any source, allowing unrelated damage to consume the shield. Restrict sources to SameObject(Source) in the Permanent source domain. Preserve the activating player identity, Any-player activation permission, NextOccurrence limit, duration, cost and replacement body. Correct the matching grammar declaration with the same complete event predicate. This is a semantic correction using existing AST operands, not a source/controller alias or schema change. Upstream repair evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/4ba5c00f . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/6 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Your next untap step retains the ability controller as both step player and expiration player.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #8 identifies 17 controller-following durations on explicitly named your-next-untap wording. Correct both DuringNextUntapStep(AbilityController) and UntapStep.players=One(AbilityController), preserving affected objects, activation/trigger identity, other changes, source, ordering and LiveObjects evaluation. Correcting only the lifetime would still let the step predicate follow a different controller, including off-turn untaps. Barl's Cage's explicit controller-following wording and Orcish Farmer's distinct controller reference remain unchanged controls. The original 17 faces are all in the explicit allowed population. These are semantic operand corrections, without a schema change or identity alias. See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/8 , published upstream repair https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/7fed1a80affa9e6ed5067210333243e3c3ada4b5 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Live untap rules on a population controlled by the ability controller use that stable player role explicitly.
updates.evidence: The same allowed wording audit also finds five land effects whose duration already names AbilityController and whose LiveObjects battlefield population is explicitly constrained by ControlledBy(One(AbilityController)). Every affected object therefore has that controller whenever the live rule applies. Its UntapStep player predicate ControllerOf(Affected) is equivalent, in precisely that proven context, to AbilityController. Normalize that predicate to the same stable named-player shape used for the other your-next-untap rules. The owned typed canonicalizer proves only this literal AbilityController implication on an exact current battlefield Zone, an explicit conjunct or whole ControlledBy predicate, one Skip rule, LiveObjects evaluation and DuringNextUntapStep(AbilityController); it bounds conjunction inspection and preserves unknown fields. It does not alias players on fixed/snapshot or unfiltered populations, change a controller-following duration, accept another player/window, or broaden the 17 actual corrections. Both replaced roles are ID-free, so no typed reference origin is removed or synthesized. Existing AST types suffice. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Juxtapose performs its independent creature and artifact exchanges in printed order.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #7: the pinned spell contains only two creature choices and their exchange. Append the independent artifact choices and exchange, preserving the first exchange, each player as chooser, maximum-mana-value eligibility, as-many-as-possible count and each exchange's separate result references. The artifact sequence is unconditional after the creature sequence, so failure or absence of the creature exchange does not suppress it. Generic shared grammar emits both complete exchanges from their current permanent kinds and player; the three former fragments that incorrectly distributed one exchange over all three printed sentences are removed. Existing AST types suffice. Published upstream witness/repair: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/4ba5c00f6e5a1b5f32abf8e017a10ccf74bd9fff . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/7 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Vexing Arcanix guards both name branches by an actual reveal and moves that observed card.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #10: an empty library still permits the prior naming choice, but provides no card for either name-comparison branch. Wrap the entire original name-test If in CountObjects(Observed(reveal_result)) >= 1, with an empty otherwise program. Naming and revealing remain outside the guard. Both moves refer to that actual Observed receipt instead of freshly querying the top library card, retaining the revealed object identity. The wrong-name damage therefore cannot occur when no card was revealed. Preserve costs, target player, name-choice domain, move destinations, source, amount and existing result IDs. This is a semantic/identity correction without an AST schema change. Published upstream repair/witnesses: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/06de9c786d700414985cb9cf960402169039b830 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/10 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Maelstrom Archangel Avatar iterates distinct damage-time creature sources instead of the current battlefield.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #14 and upstream contract clarification #125: creature/controller predicates apply when combat damage was dealt to a player this turn. Replace the current Battlefield population with Union([FromHistory(Damage{source_kind:Permanent,sources:Creature AND ControlledBy(AbilityController),recipients:Players(All),kind:Combat,grouping:Source,subject:Source},ThisTurn)]). The set union deduplicates repeated events for the same source identity. Departed creatures and later control changes cannot alter which historical participants qualify. Preserve loop binding, mana-COST matching (not mana value), random selection, copy operations, optional payment and all result identities. No schema change or source/current-controller equality alias. Published corrected lowering and scoped regressions: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/123fb91240db27e8396a24bd10274ce9d1618183 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/14 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Maelstrom Archangel Avatar tests both printed chosen-copy types explicitly.
updates.evidence: While correcting issue #14, the same pinned body was found to lower two positive printed conditions into one If/else: any failure of the permanent test offered the spell-casting branch, including when no copy was chosen. Preserve the permanent then-program with an empty otherwise, and add the explicit Instant OR Sorcery chosen-copy condition with the original casting program and an empty otherwise. Both printed conditions now retain their own meanings; no missing/other-kind copy falls into an unconditional cast branch. Keep optional payment and choice ordering, actor, copy identities, result IDs and all body operands. The grammar also fixes formerly unrepresented count words to the actual single-copy wording and checks agreement between the loop noun and its repeated noun; edited costs and loop kinds still derive from current operands. This is a semantic lowering correction using existing AST types, not an equivalence normalization. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md and https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/14 .

updates.summary: Direct least-power destruction chooses a destructible member of the already computed minimum pool.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #12: Drop of Honey and Porphyry Nodes instruct destruction directly, so CR609.3 requires doing as much as possible. Preserve the complete existing creature/minimum-power population, then apply Not(HasKeyword(Indestructible)) outside that population before selecting. Do not filter the Aggregate Minimum input: an indestructible least-power creature must not make a higher-power creature eligible. Preserve the controller chooser, AsManyAsCan(1), result addresses and no-regeneration destruction. Imperial Edict's separate choose instruction remains unrestricted by this direct-destruction legality filter. Published primary lowering/runtime-witness evidence: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/2e6c5d6008fe90c72da86393e56f568a2a43f492 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/12 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md. Existing AST types suffice.

updates.summary: Frankenstein's Monster performs an as-much-as-possible exile effect and checks actual exile arrivals.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #13: the entering instruction is an effect governed by CR609.3, not an indivisible cost under CR118.3. Replace mandatory PayCost(Move Exactly X) with WithSelections choosing AsManyAsCan(X), followed by the actual exile Move. Compare the number of actual After transitions arriving in Exile to the entering object's CastX; if incomplete, retain the original owner-graveyard entry redirect. The counter amount counts actual creature-card arrivals in the same receipt. Use Matching(Transition{After},InZone(Exile)) on the recorded arrival incarnation, not ObjectSet::InZone current membership, not requested inputs and not a fresh zone query. Redirected arrivals do not count, while later movement cannot erase a recorded exile arrival. Preserve the entering controller, selection population, counter kinds/choice semantics, destinations and instruction identities; real costs are unchanged. Existing schema-190 types suffice. Published primary repairs/witnesses: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/2e6c5d6008fe90c72da86393e56f568a2a43f492 and https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/9ffdb82199daa30db62113eeb2ab42b0cef5ea85 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/13 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Post-destroy characteristic tests retain the original target independently of successful destruction.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #9: Thermokarst and Extinguish the Light test the targeted permanent even when destruction fails. Replace the successful-destroy Result{Before,index0} condition operand with the actual Target reference from the preceding instruction, retaining its current/last-known identity, filter, comparison, reward and all other operands. The shared grammar had an incorrect comment/meaning treating a performed-action Before receipt as attempted input; it now repeats the captured target explicitly instead. This is a semantic identity correction, not a Result/Target equality alias. No schema change. Published upstream repair/witnesses: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/06de9c786d700414985cb9cf960402169039b830 . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/9 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Wand of Ith tests an observed nonland in its second branch.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #15 and upstream https://github.com/i5jb/mtgish/issues/285: the printed second branch says it is not a land. Keep the CountObjects(Matching(Observed(reveal), filter)) >= 1 existence test and negate only CardType(Land) inside its filter. Both positive land and positive nonland existence tests remain false on an empty reveal; do not negate the whole existence test. Preserve random reveal, target player, both optional payments, original life amounts and mana-value expression, payment receipts, discard actions and activation restriction. This corrects actual condition operands in the reference and grammar, using existing schema 190 types. Native upstream witnesses distinguish declined nonland payment, paid nonland and a land that cannot receive a second prompt. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Each drawing player reads their own shuffled-card receipt after the separate all-player shuffle phase.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #16: Winds of Change, Molten Psyche and Whirlpool Warrior must not draw the combined total for each player. Keep the original first all-player shuffle loop; replace the following global Draw with a separate ForEachPlayer(All) loop whose Draw recipient and MovedBy{result:shuffle,phase:Before,player} use the same bound player. Count actual original shuffled cards and preserve identities and result addresses. Never interleave one player's shuffle/draw before the next shuffle. Preserve Molten Psyche's metalcraft/damage and the Warrior's separate single-player trigger. Credit Voucher and Whirlpool Rider retain their normal single-player Transition receipts; Psychic Spiral's target still mills the caster's shuffled count. Source was already correct; this is a lowering correction, not a Source rewrite or equivalence normalization. Existing schema 190 concepts suffice. Primary published implementation, decision note and six-face regressions: https://github.com/vishvananda/mtgish/commit/6deb7e262e2a2681dea301951b6dac46f2c41d9a . Native generated-code witness publication is recorded on issue #16; not rerun here. See docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Total War tests attacks during the current combat, retaining its separate turn-long control exemption.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #17: the printed attack trigger destroys eligible nonattackers in that combat. A source that attacked in a previous combat must not be protected during an additional combat. Change only the candidate attack EventHistory window from ThisTurn to ThisCombat; keep the attacking player's identity, untapped/non-Wall/creature filters, continuous-control-since-turn-began exception, batching and destruction. Explicit 'this turn' predicates elsewhere remain ThisTurn. This changes an observable historical operand, not an equivalence shape. Existing schema 190 HistoryWindow::ThisCombat suffices. The report records a distinguishing retained Aurelia additional-combat native scenario; not rerun in this frontend. See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/17 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md.

updates.summary: Shapeshifter's intrinsic chosen-number power/toughness formula is a characteristic-defining ability.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #18: the final printed definition and */7-* power/toughness meet CR604.3/604.3a. Replace the Ordinary Static plus split SetPower/SetToughness with CharacteristicDefining and SetBasePowerToughness over the same ChosenNumber and Subtract(7,ChosenNumber) formula. A CDA functions in every zone and applies in layer7a (CR613.4a); ordinary self-setting effects remain ordinary. An undetermined chosen number uses zero (CR107.2), without collapsing the stored symbolic formula or clamping values. Preserve entering controller, both number choices, optional upkeep choice, source identity and all numeric operands. The grammar uses the existing context-aware defining_static contract, rather than globally reclassifying setters or marking granted/conditional effects intrinsic. Existing schema190 types suffice. Official rules: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020261106.pdf . See https://github.com/vishvananda/oracle-grammar/issues/18 and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md; reported native hand-state witness is not rerun here.

updates.summary: Arboria tests who put the permanent onto the battlefield during the named player's last completed turn.
updates.evidence: Repository issue #11 and merged model PR #3: PlayerHistory::PermanentEntered observes the entering controller, whereas the printed put action observes the actor. Replace only that second predicate with EventHistory(Player{PutsOntoBattlefield, players:One(the_bound_player), objects:Not(Token)}, HistoryWindow::LastTurnOf(the_same_player), Occurrences) >= 1. Keep the cast-spell alternative, creature attack restriction, player matching scopes and nontoken population. LastTurnOf denotes that player's most recent completed turn, not the preceding global turn or SinceLastTurnOf; no previous turn yields no occurrence. This requires schema191 / packages0.2.0. Corpus preparation first uses the owned frozen-schema migration from190 to191, then applies this amendment, so the new variant never carries a190 header. Published0.1.0 and pinnedexport/reference-lock remain immutable. See docs/named-player-history.md and docs/reported-issues-20261113.md. Source's put form was already correct; no upstream text rewrite or controller/actor equality alias is introduced.

updates.summary: Octomancer's gift creates one 8/8 blue Octopus, independently of the article's count.
updates.evidence: The allowed original Oracle reminder explicitly defines an 8/8 blue Octopus. CR702.174i defines the same intrinsic gift effect: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020261106.pdf . The pinned lowering and its mined template instead reuse the article 'an' as both token amount and power/toughness, making a 1/1. Change only those two stat expressions from Constant(1) to Constant(8); retain one token, GiftedPlayer, Blue/Creature/Octopus, untapped entry and the separate end-step copy trigger. The shared grammar declares this closed gift definition, rather than inferring stats from a count word. This corrects AST operands, not schema or an equality normalization. See the gift simplification notes.

updates.summary: Use AnnouncedX consistently for a spell-own casting value in its conditions and target distribution.
updates.evidence: These 28 numeric operands on 21 allowed faces query Source.SpellX in the same Spell frame whose other amounts and filters use AnnouncedX for the identical chosen X. CR107.3a defines that casting choice; CR707.10 preserves it when a spell is copied. Normalize only this own-spell value, including its announcement/distribution; retain thresholds, comparisons, branches, player/object identities and result IDs. Independent abilities, costs, delayed/reflexive/replacement programs, CastX history, EventActivationX, explicit other objects and captured values are excluded from the frontend normalization. No global Source/holder alias or schema change. Original Oracle wording is unchanged. Official rules: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020261106.pdf . See docs/spell-x-thresholds.md.

updates.summary: Measure a proved single activation exile receipt as that card, consistently with ordinary object properties.
updates.evidence: The allowed original Oracle texts name the mana value of one exiled card (Ellie and Alan) or creature (Food Chain). Both activation costs have one direct Move-to-Exile component with one selection choosing Exactly(Constant(1)); their existing operands sum ManaValue over that same Activation/Performed/After receipt. A sum over this proved singleton is its one card property, with CurrentOrLastKnown information, as in the existing singleton transition-receipt lowering. Keep the exact payment component, receipt phase, property, and all other operands; no zone query or persistent exiled-with alias is introduced. The frontend extends the existing singleton-receipt proof and reversible surface projection to these exact cost components. Other payment kinds, phases, views, plural or optional selections, malformed inputs and independent ability scopes are excluded. See docs/copiable-abilities-and-actions.md and src/bind/single_receipts.rs.

updates.summary: Use the immediate whole-hand observation for card choices that query the same revealed hand.
updates.evidence: These 79 operands on 78 allowed faces choose cards immediately after revealing that same complete hand. The old records query its current hand; other records and the shared observation grammar select from the revealed receipt, guarded by Hand and that same owner. With no intervening instruction or scope change, these represent the same population. Normalize only adjacent native Reveal(Zone Players Hand, Card, Any) followed by ChooseObjects from the identical one-player Hand/Card zone. Keep eligibility, count, chooser, selected/discard/exile receipts and other instructions. CR400.3 assigns hand cards to their owner; https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260619.pdf . The owned bounded canonicalizer proves the same identity and preserves origin annotations, invalid fields and duplicate definitions; partial observations, other hands, intervening actions and independent frames do not acquire that receipt. See docs/nonlegendary-and-observed-hands.md.

updates.summary: Represent a plain distinct exchange pair as one two-object target group.
updates.evidence: Six plain Spell frames on four allowed faces exchange two permanents with identical target-free eligibility. Their old representation uses two required singleton slots, with an explicit Not(SameObject(first target)) on the second. This selects exactly the same distinct pair as one Exactly(2) target group. Preserve the first object at index 0 and map the second object to index 1; preserve the full eligibility, action, actor and surrounding abilities. Only a single ExchangeControl action, ordinary battlefield object domains and empty target metadata qualify. Different/target-dependent filters, optional counts, constraints, modal announcements and other instructions do not establish this proof. The owned typed, bounded normalizer validates lossless native input, keeps independent Spell/Spree scopes separate and carries coalesced declaration and operand origins. This is a semantic normal form change with no wire schema change. CR115.3: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020260619.pdf . See docs/copy-exceptions-and-exchange-pairs.md.

updates.summary: Death Charmer makes the damaged creature's controller lose the life they decline to pay for.
updates.evidence: The Oracle trigger says "that creature's controller loses 2 life unless they pay {2}". The pinned IR offers the payment to ControllerOf(Damage(Recipient)) but its LoseLife names One(AbilityController), so the Worm's own controller would lose the life. The player who loses life is the "they" who may pay, as in every other "<player> loses N life unless they pay" record (Elesh Norn, and the cast and draw triggers that use EventSubject for both). Only the LoseLife player changes; the payment, its optional flag, the PaymentChosen test and the damage event stay intact.

updates.summary: Snowfall lets a snow Island's controller add one or two additional blue mana, not only two.
updates.evidence: The Oracle trigger says "its controller may add an additional {U}. If that Island is snow, its controller may add an additional {U}{U} instead." The "instead" is optional (CR614.1a, 614.15, 616.1): declining it keeps the first option of one additional {U}, so a snow Island offers zero, one or two. The pinned IR's snow Optional body adds two {U} only. It becomes a ChooseOne of one or two {U}. The nonsnow body, the Optional decider, the tapped Island's controller as recipient and the cumulative-upkeep spending rule stay intact. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#25 (source report i5jb/mtgish#289).

updates.summary: Aladdin's Lamp leaves the card it keeps in place instead of putting it back on top.
updates.evidence: The Oracle replacement says "look at the top X cards of your library, put all but one of them on the bottom of your library in a random order, then draw a card." It never moves the retained card. The pinned IR adds ReorderLibrary(Top) of the selected card, an action the text doesn't print. The bottom step then excludes that action's input. The correction drops the ReorderLibrary(Top) and excludes Selected(2) from the random bottom order directly. LookAt, the ChooseObjects of one card as possible, the random bottom order, the cancelled draw and the real Draw stay intact. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#26.

updates.summary: Bison Whistle offers its four choices for any looked-at card, so a creature card may go to the graveyard.
updates.evidence: The Oracle ability says "If it's a Bison card, you may put it onto the battlefield. If it's a creature card, you may reveal it and put it into your hand. Otherwise, you may put it into your graveyard." The MTGish maintainer clarified on i5jb/mtgish#169 that after looking, the controller may choose the battlefield for a Bison, the hand for a creature, the graveyard for any card after declining those, or leave the card on top. The pinned IR wraps the menu in an If(Bison or creature) test and offers the graveyard only when that test fails. The correction replaces the If with one ChooseOne of four options: Bison to the battlefield, creature revealed to hand, the unrestricted top card to the graveyard, and nothing. The LookAt and every option's operation stay intact. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#27.

updates.summary: Scholarship Sponsor and Enigma Ridges subtract each searching player's lands from the most lands, not the reverse.
updates.evidence: Both Oracle texts search for "a number of basic land cards less than or equal to the difference" between the most lands any player controls and the fewer lands of each searching player. The pinned IR computes Subtract([lands of Bound(0), BoundValue(0)]), which is never positive for an eligible player. The correction reverses the operands to Subtract([BoundValue(0), lands of Bound(0)]). The captured maximum, player eligibility, basic-land filter, up-to count, Scholarship Sponsor's tapped arrival, Enigma Ridges' reveal and hand destination, the shuffles and Enigma Ridges' chaos ability stay intact. MTGish accepted the reversed subtraction on i5jb/mtgish#172. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#28.

updates.summary: Boreas Charger counts the difference in lands, not in hand sizes.
updates.evidence: The Oracle trigger says "choose an opponent who controls more lands than you. Search your library for a number of Plains cards equal to the difference". The difference is between the two players' lands, which the choice also compares. The pinned IR subtracts the AbilityController's hand size from the chosen opponent's. The correction counts lands on the battlefield controlled by Chosen minus lands controlled by AbilityController. The chosen opponent, the Plains filter, the reveal, the one tapped battlefield arrival, the rest to hand and the shuffle stay intact. Sandstone Oracle and Slithermuse compare hand sizes and stay unchanged. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#28 (i5jb/mtgish#172).

updates.summary: Heroism offers each attacking red creature's payment as the ability resolves, and its shield names that creature.
updates.evidence: The Oracle ability says "For each attacking red creature, prevent all combat damage that would be dealt by that creature this turn unless its controller pays {2}{R}." The Wizards ruling of 2004-10-04 places the payment on resolution, once for each creature attacking then. The pinned IR instead creates one shield for any attacking red creature and asks for the payment inside it each time damage would be dealt, so later attackers and repeated damage events are admitted. The correction loops over the attacking red creatures as the ability resolves, offers {2}{R} to each one's controller, and creates a shield for that same creature unless it was paid. The sacrifice cost, the combat damage event, its recipients and grouping, the end-of-turn duration and the prevention stay intact. The order of the payments follows the ForEachObject choice-order contract. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#23.

updates.summary: Tokens created with a permanent are tokens, not every object one of its abilities put onto the battlefield.
updates.evidence: Arcane Artisan, Dance of Many, Dual Nature, Saproling Burst, Tetravus and Tombstone Stairwell name "tokens created with" the permanent or "the token" it created. The pinned IR uses MadeBy(Source) alone, which the model defines as created or put onto the battlefield by an ability of this object, so it also admits a nontoken put onto the battlefield by such an ability (a Tetravus given Starfleet Communicator's attack trigger puts an Island onto the battlefield and would offer it for exile). Each reference gains a Token intersection, as Faerie Artisans' record already has for "other tokens created with this creature". The cross-ability link to the printed creating ability (CR 607.2c) is a separate, open question. The same token-type correction is in vishvananda/mtgish@639c2ea9. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#20.

updates.summary: Inside PlayersDo, the acting player is PlayerRef::Acting and AbilityController stays the ability's controller, as in EachPlayer.
updates.evidence: The pinned export names the acting player inside PlayersDo inconsistently. Ingenious Mastery's opponent creates the Treasures and scries for AbilityController, and the shuffle on Natural Selection, Portent and Visions, Cloudhoof Kirin's mill and Stardew Valley's control change also read AbilityController as the acting player. Protection Racket reads the other way: "your library" inside its PlayersDo is the original AbilityController. Thought Prison mixes both: the target player's hand is AbilityController, and so is "you" who chooses from it. Infernal Denizen needs both identities at once: the opponent chooses and gains control, while the eligible creatures stay controlled by the original controller. The model already documents PlayerRef::Acting as the player doing the action inside EachPlayer, and oracle-ir now documents PlayersDo the same way: Acting is the acting player and AbilityController is the controller of the ability, including inside the body. Each change replaces only the AbilityController that names the actor: the opponent who creates and scries (Ingenious Mastery), the player who shuffles or mills, the player who gains control (Stardew Valley, Infernal Denizen), the opponent who chooses (Infernal Denizen) and the target player's revealed hand and its owner (Thought Prison). "You" stays AbilityController: Infernal Denizen's creatures you control, Thought Prison's chooser, and the Treasure's own mana ability, which is a separate ability. Protection Racket and every PlayersDo performed by the ability's controller already read this way and are unchanged. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#24.

updates.summary: Drach'Nyen sums the current power of every card exiled with it, including exiled noncreature cards such as Vehicles.
updates.evidence: "X is the exiled card's power" reads the cards linked to the enter trigger. A copied trigger can exile several cards, and CR 607.3 then sums the variable answers, as U0008 does for Phyrexian Ingester. The old operand reads Query index zero of an unordered exile population. Unlike Ingester's "exiled creature card", Drach'Nyen says "the exiled card": a Vehicle that was animated when exiled is a noncreature card in exile but still has a printed power (CR 208.3), so the population keeps every linked card and adds no Creature conjunct. Rules: https://media.wizards.com/2026/downloads/MagicCompRules%2020261106.pdf (607.3, 208.3). Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#30.

updates.summary: Protection Racket's payer is the acting opponent, PlayerRef::Acting, not Prior(That).
updates.evidence: The Oracle trigger says "repeat the following process for each opponent in turn order. Reveal the top card of your library. That player may pay life equal to that card's mana value." The pinned record runs the process in PlayersDo over the controller's opponents and names the payer Prior(That), "whichever the row around this one names", while the reveal in the same body names the controller's library. Inside PlayersDo the player doing the actions is PlayerRef::Acting (U0046), so the payer is Acting. The library, the life amount, the payment choice and both destinations stay intact. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#24.

updates.summary: "You may have target player [act]" is the controller's choice, Instruction::Optional with decider AbilityController around the target player's action.
updates.evidence: PlayersDo's optional flag did not say who declines. In the pinned export it is the acting player for Infernal Denizen's "an opponent may" and Stardew Valley's "another player of your choice may", and the controller for "you may have target player" on Cloudhoof Kirin, Natural Selection, Portent, Thought Prison and Visions. Twenty-one other "you may have target player" records, such as Dire Undercurrents and Disciple of the Vault, already use Optional{decider: AbilityController} around the target's action. These five follow them, with the acting player written as the target, so PlayersDo's optional flag is only the acting players' own choice. The look, reorder, mill amount, revealed hand, nonland choice, exile and shuffle stay intact. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#24.

updates.summary: Frankenstein's Monster and Mimeoplasm, Revered One choose the creature cards with ChooseObjects and exile Selected, as other effects that exile cards from a graveyard do.
updates.evidence: "As this creature enters, exile X creature cards from your graveyard" (Frankenstein's Monster) and "exile up to X creature cards from your graveyard" (Mimeoplasm) are one action that picks its own objects. Fifty-five other records choose graveyard cards with ChooseObjects and exile Selected(choice), among them Living Lore and Sutured Ghoul, whose "As this creature enters, exile ... from your graveyard" is the same entering replacement. Among entering replacements, only these two use WithSelections. The choice happens immediately before the move, with nothing between them, so the selection and the move receipt correspond exactly. The chooser, the population, the count (AsManyAsCan(X) or UpTo(X)), the exile destination, the number of cards actually exiled (read from the move's Transition receipt), the counters and Frankenstein's Monster's graveyard destination stay intact. Reported in vishvananda/oracle-grammar#29.

updates.summary: Ignite Memories reveals a card at random from the target player's hand with RevealFromHand and reads it as Observed, as the other random hand reveals do.
updates.evidence: "Target player reveals a card at random from their hand. Ignite Memories deals damage to that player equal to that card's mana value" has no cost and no "if you do". Eighteen other records encode a random reveal from hand as RevealFromHand{at_random:true}, among them Planeswalker's Fury and Planeswalker's Mirth, whose "Target opponent reveals a card at random from their hand" is followed by the same "equal to that card's mana value" and reads the card as Query{Observed(reveal), 0}. Only Ignite Memories encoded it as a mandatory PayCost{Reveal{random:true}} followed by If PaymentChosen. The target player, the damage source, recipient and preventability, the mana value read and the Storm ability stay intact.

updates.summary: Rotfeaster Maggot gains life equal to the exiled target card's toughness, read from the Target as other "target card ... that card's" records do, not an unresolved Earlier exile.
updates.evidence: In "exile target creature card from a graveyard. You gain life equal to that card's toughness", that card is the target the first sentence exiled. The record measured Earlier{what:Exiled, result:null}, a placeholder that names no exile. Records with the same shape read the target: Surge to Victory ("Exile target instant or sorcery card from your graveyard ... where X is that card's mana value"), Healing Technique, Phyrexian Delver, Pyretic Rebirth, Razor Hippogriff and Volcanic Vision measure ObjectProperty{object:Target{slot:0}}. The trigger, target, exile and life gain stay intact.

updates.summary: Hesitation triggers when any player casts a spell, as "When a player casts a spell" reads in every other record, not only when its controller does.
updates.evidence: "A player" names no particular player. Of 116 reference triggers written "When a player casts" or "Whenever a player casts", 115 record the casting players as All, among them Standstill ("When a player casts a spell, sacrifice this enchantment") and Norin the Wary. Hesitation alone recorded One(AbilityController). The sacrifice and counter stay intact.

updates.summary: Voltage Surge and Undergrowth are one cost branch on their optional additional cost, as the other spells that test "this spell's additional cost was paid" are recorded.
updates.evidence: Fourteen spells that offer an optional additional cost and then ask whether it was paid are recorded as one CostBranch{keyword: AdditionalCost} with a paid and an unpaid spell, among them Burning Curiosity and Cinder Strike ("you may blight 1 ... if this spell's additional cost was paid") and Osseous Exhale ("you may behold a Dragon ... If a Dragon was beheld"). Voltage Surge and Undergrowth alone recorded a separate optional Casting additional cost and a Spell testing ObjectMatches{Source, State(CostPaid(Additional))}. The normalization makes each one CostBranch: the paid spell is the If's then branch and the unpaid spell its otherwise branch. The costs ({2}{R}; sacrificing an artifact), Voltage Surge's target and both damage amounts, and Undergrowth's two combat damage preventions stay intact. Graven Archfiend and Katara, Seeking Revenge are permanents whose later abilities test the paid cost, and stay unchanged.

updates.summary: Chameleon Spirit's power and toughness ability is characteristic-defining, as the other creatures whose power and toughness count a value chosen as they enter are recorded.
updates.evidence: CR 604.3: a static ability printed on a card that sets its power and toughness is a characteristic-defining ability and functions in all zones. Six other records whose power or toughness counts a value chosen as the creature enters are CharacteristicDefining, among them Entropic Specter, Lost Order of Jarkeld, Pallimud and Skyshroud War Beast. Chameleon Spirit alone recorded an Ordinary static. Its SetBasePowerToughness change and the counted permanents of the chosen color stay intact.

updates.summary: "Another ... spell this turn" tested while this spell is cast excludes this spell, as the casting restrictions written the same way are recorded.
updates.evidence: Nine records of "you've cast another [quality] spell this turn" exclude the source with Not(SameObject(Source)), among them Dream Thief, Soul Reap and the casting restrictions of Hewed Stone Retainers, Illusory Angel, Skyshroud Condor and Talara's Battalion ("Cast this spell only if you've cast another spell this turn"), which are also tested while the spell is cast. Gigastorm Titan and Rally the Monastery ("This spell costs ... less to cast if you've cast another spell this turn"), Mage Duel ("another instant or sorcery spell") and Patrician's Scorn ("If you've cast another white spell this turn, you may cast this spell without paying its mana cost") recorded the bare spell filter. The normalization adds Not(SameObject(Source)) to each. Sage of the Skies tests the history from its cast trigger and excludes the triggering spell, Not(SameObject(EventSubject)); it stays unchanged.

updates.summary: Chief Magistrate of Mercadia copies each creature token its controller controls, as "for each creature token you control" says, not each creature.
updates.evidence: "Then if you're the monarch, for each creature token you control, create a token that's a copy of it." The CopyEach population recorded creatures you control and dropped the Token filter. Rhys the Redeemed ("For each creature token you control, create a token that's a copy of that creature") records the same words as AllOf([CardType(Creature), Token, ControlledBy(You)]).

updates.summary: Kimahri, Valiant Guardian is what becomes a copy of the tapped creature, as "you may have Kimahri become a copy of that creature" says.
updates.evidence: The copy effect recorded the target creature as the affected object, so the target would become a copy of itself. The sentence's subject is Kimahri, and the exceptions (its name is Kimahri, Valiant Guardian; it has vigilance and this ability) describe Kimahri. Cryptoplasm, Protean Thaumaturge and Sunfrill Imitator ("you may have this creature become a copy of ... target creature") record the source as affected and the target as the copied object.

updates.summary: Renegade Doppelganger's copy keeps no exception; its reminder text says the copy loses this ability.
updates.evidence: "You may have this creature become a copy of that creature until end of turn. (If it does, it loses this ability for the rest of the turn.)" A copy takes the copied creature's abilities (CR 707.2), so the creature loses this triggered ability, as the reminder says. The record kept it with AddCurrentAbility, which the 22 other records with that exception write as "except it has this ability" (Cryptoplasm, Protean Thaumaturge).

updates.summary: A choice among cards in exile names the exile pool itself, as most records of such choices write it, without restating that those cards are in exile.
updates.evidence: 33 records write a choice among exiled cards as Zone(Shared(Exile)) with its filter, among them Ashiok, Nightmare Weaver, Ethereal Forager, Koh, the Face Stealer and Tomb of the Dusk Rose. 18 records wrapped the same pool in InZone(..., Exile), which tests again that cards already in exile are in exile, so both forms choose among the same cards. Bane Alley Broker's "return a card exiled with this creature to its owner's hand" is wrapped while Ethereal Forager's "return an instant or sorcery card exiled with this creature to its owner's hand" is not. The normalization drops the wrapper; each pool's filter and count stay unchanged. Moves of exiled cards keep InZone, as 73 records write them.

updates.summary: Kenessos, Priest of Thassa and Lantern of Revealing let their controller choose whether to put the declined card on the bottom, as "you may put it on the bottom of your library" says.
updates.evidence: "If you don't put the card onto the battlefield, you may put it on the bottom of your library." Both records made the bottom move mandatory and dropped the choice. Bucolic Ranch ("If you don't put it into your hand, you may put it on the bottom of your library") and Cabaretti Ascendancy record the same words as an Optional move decided by the ability's controller.

updates.summary: Fecund Greenshell triggers only when another creature you control enters, as "another creature you control with toughness greater than its power enters" says.
updates.evidence: "Whenever this creature or another creature you control with toughness greater than its power enters, look at the top card of your library." The record's second event accepted any such creature entering, under any player's control, and dropped "you control". Risen Reef ("Whenever this creature or another Elemental you control enters") records the same words with ControlledBy(You) in the entering creature's filter.

updates.summary: Nissa's Revelation reads the power and toughness of the card it revealed from that reveal, as revealed-card values are recorded elsewhere.
updates.evidence: "Scry 5, then reveal the top card of your library. If it's a creature card, you draw cards equal to its power and you gain life equal to its toughness." The record's test already names the reveal as Observed(1), but both amounts used Earlier{what:Revealed}, a placeholder that names no result. 36 records read a revealed card's value as ObjectProperty{object:Query{Observed(reveal), 0}, information:CurrentOrLastKnown}, among them Ad Nauseam. The normalization names the same reveal; the draw, the life gain and the test stay unchanged.

updates.summary: Disruptor Flute taxes every spell with the chosen name, whoever casts it, as "Spells with the chosen name cost {3} more to cast" says.
updates.evidence: "Spells with the chosen name cost {3} more to cast." names no caster, but the record taxed only spells its controller cast, so an opponent's copy of the named card cost nothing extra. Gloom ("White spells cost {3} more to cast") and Thalia, Guardian of Thraben record the same unqualified wording for every player. Where the words do name a caster, the record adds it: Anointed Peacekeeper ("Spells your opponents cast with the chosen name") has Cast{by:OpponentsOf(You)}, and Brago's Favor ("you cast") has Cast{by:You}. The correction keeps the effect on the chosen name's spells and drops the caster.

updates.summary: Kindred Charge copies only creatures you control of the chosen type, as "For each creature you control of the chosen type" says.
updates.evidence: "Choose a creature type. For each creature you control of the chosen type, create a token that's a copy of that creature." The record's copied set kept the creature type and the chosen type but dropped "you control", so it copied every player's creatures of that type. Rhys the Redeemed ("For each creature token you control, create a token that's a copy of that creature"), Second Harvest and Saheeli, the Gifted record the same words with ControlledBy(AbilityController).

updates.summary: Molten Echoes and Mordor on the March name the copy token they created as that creation's batch, as the same follow-up words are recorded elsewhere.
updates.evidence: Molten Echoes ("create a token that's a copy of that creature. That token gains haste. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step.") and Mordor on the March ("Create a token that's a copy of it. It gains haste until end of turn. Exile it at the beginning of the next end step.") recorded the grant and the delayed exile on One(Result{index:0}), the first object of the creation. Flameshadow Conjuring records Molten Echoes' exact follow-up as Created(creation); Felhide Spiritbinder, Cadric, Soul Kindler, Mishra, Eminent One and Séance do the same for "It gains haste" and "Exile/Sacrifice it at the beginning of the next end step". A replacement effect can make one requested token several, and the batch covers each of them.

updates.summary: Lazotep Quarry, Nahiri, the Unforgiving and The Scarab God copy the target they exiled as "Create a token that's a copy of it" is recorded elsewhere.
updates.evidence: Each exiles one target creature (or Equipment) card from a graveyard, then says "Create a token that's a copy of it". The three records copied the exile's result, Result{index:0}. Restore Relic ("Exile target artifact or creature card from your graveyard. Create a token that's a copy of it."), The Cloning of Shredder and Abyssal Harvester record the same "copy of it" on the exiled Target; the copy reads the same copiable values either way. Records that say "a copy of that card" (Anikthea, Hand of Erebos, Offspring's Revenge, Tamiyo, Compleated Sage) keep the exile receipt, as the grammar reads that phrase.

updates.summary: Preserve the five Gates' printed manifestations of their intrinsic basic-land mana abilities.
updates.evidence: Gate to Manorborn ("Land — Forest Gate") prints "This land enters tapped.", its activated seek ability and "{T}: Add {G}." as three lines, without reminder parentheses; Gate of the Black Dragon, Gate to Seatower, Gate to Tumbledown and Gate to the Citadel print the same for their basic land types. The records kept two abilities and dropped the printed mana line. Abandoned Air Temple ("{T}: Add {W}."), Agadeem, the Undercrypt and Ba Sing Se record each printed mana line as an Activated AddMana ability. Issue #32 clarifies that these lines preserve wording only: CR 305.6 derives the mana abilities from the current basic land types even when their text is absent. The owned contract's intrinsic projection recognizes only the exact plain tap-for-one activation on a land with that type; consumers combine its nonintrinsic printed abilities with one derived ability per current type. It does not coalesce independently granted abilities, restricted mana, additional costs, different recipients or modified activations. Unprinted intrinsic abilities are not added to the written list.

updates.summary: Count only Mimeoplasm's recorded Exile arrivals when adding entry counters.
updates.evidence: Issue #31; the Move/Transition arrival contract retains actual destination zones after replacement. The chosen objects are not the successful Exile arrivals. Match Creature and Exile against the recorded After view; later moves do not erase that recorded arrival, and a redirected Hand arrival contributes no counters. Preserve the move result and multiplier three; this is not a current-zone membership test.

updates.summary: Remove redundant zone membership from five live Exile queries in four linked-card faces.
updates.evidence: Issue #33 follows U0060. Each inner ObjectSet::Zone already queries Shared(Exile), so the enclosing InZone(..., Exile) adds no predicate. Preserve ExiledWith(Source), every other filter, the chooser, movement and count. This proof does not apply to Observed, Selected, Transition, Take or an arbitrary object set, and never removes a recorded arrival-zone qualification.

updates.summary: Use proved singleton and immediate reveal-observation operands consistently.
updates.evidence: Issue #33: Chandra exiles exactly the top one card and plays that actual move result; Matching(One(Result(0, After, 0)), Any) adds no constraint. Esper Maduin reveals its own library top, then its pure permanent-card condition moves that observed card with no intervening effect. Preserve the explicit library player and reveal result. This does not equate arbitrary multi-card receipts with index zero or live library queries with observations; intervening effects and different library players invalidate the observation proof. The same adjacent one-card Reveal/If proof applies to 49 branch moves on the 32 explicitly listed allowed faces. Every condition already consumes that reveal observation; only the first effect through pure If/Optional branches moves the identical top query. The bounded contract reduction and its print inverse implement this proof rather than choosing faces by name.

updates.summary: Keep each listed mana-color mapping in one replacement effect with applicable output choices.
updates.evidence: Issue #19 and the 2004-10-04 / 2013-04-15 rulings retained in the report; independently reviewed native capability in cantrip-rs/cantrip-rs#3007. One sentence creates one replacement identity. Options test the proposed source's current, text-adjusted types; its tapping player chooses one applicable type for all of the produced mana. No eligible option makes this replacement inapplicable. Preserve cumulative upkeep and other replacements' ordinary ordering; this effect cannot apply again to its own event.

updates.summary: Bind Tetravus's created-token selector to its linked creating ability and acquisition.
updates.evidence: Issue #20; CR 607.2c and 607.5. Generic MadeBy(Source) includes unrelated granted abilities and separate acquisitions. CreatedWith(Source) names the current consuming ability's linked text/acquisition on that exact source incarnation. Preserve the Token intersection, optional exile payment and actual-payment counter quantity. Current-resolution Created(result) and generic MadeBy remain separate relations.

updates.summary: Project Krovikan Vampire's qualifying deaths to their first surviving graveyard incarnations.
updates.evidence: Issue #21 and CR 400.7. Evaluate Creature and damage-history predicates against each departed battlefield object's historical view, then project its first graveyard incarnation only while it remains there. Recompute deaths this turn at resolution, including a qualifying death in response. Do not flatten the pre-death predicate into a current graveyard CardType query, redefine FromHistory, or revive a link after a second zone change. Preserve the returned population's movement receipt and delayed sacrifice.

updates.summary: Retain Wood Elemental's linked entry-sacrifice history instead of an unanchored preceding count.
updates.evidence: Issue #22, including the independently reviewed entry-sacrifice witness in cantrip-rs/cantrip-rs#3006. Count actual historical sacrifices linked to this entering incarnation and ability acquisition, testing their historical characteristics through the source's current text. A text change from Forest to Island must re-evaluate the filter; no chosen-number tally or contextual Earlier value suffices. Failed entries, unrelated sacrifices, copies and later incarnations do not inherit the witness. Dracoplasm's immediate Transition(Before) sums already retain its actual local sacrifice receipts and are unchanged.

updates.summary: Use the existing proved singleton convention after vacuous receipt filters disappear.
updates.evidence: Issue #33 producer consistency. Inscribed Tablet moves at most its one selected library card into hand; its After receipt has at most one arrival. Kaervek's Purge, Kalitas and Saw in Half each destroy exactly one announced target and test the successful Before receipt. A nonempty receipt test and ObjectMatches(Result(result, phase, 0), Any) therefore have the same truth value, including an empty receipt. Keep each original result, phase, negation and later effect. The shared frontend receipt proof already requires at most one object; two-card and replaceable mill batches do not qualify. This is a finite recorded normalization, not a global count/index-zero alias.

updates.summary: Lizard, Connors's Curse replaces card types with Creature without retaining other types.
updates.evidence: Lizard, Connors's Curse says "up to one other target creature loses all abilities and becomes a green Lizard creature with base power and toughness 4/4." Under CR 205.1a, because the effect does not say "in addition to its other types", it sets the target's card types to Creature (removing Artifact, Enchantment, etc. on multi-type creatures), matching Oko, Thief of Crowns ("loses all abilities and becomes a green Elk creature with base power and toughness 3/3", which already records SetCardTypes([Creature])). The pinned reference recorded AddCardType(Creature).

updates.summary: Preserve the triggering or targeted player identity rather than substituting AbilityController.
updates.evidence: Bamboozle puts the rest on top of 'their [target player's] library', not AbilityController's; Blinkmoth Urn triggers at 'each player's first main phase', not only AbilityController's; Cheering Crowd, Cruel Reality, and Paradox Haze act on the triggering player (EventSubject), not AbilityController; Sleep skips untapping during 'that player's next untap step' (Target(0,0)), not ControllerOf(Affected).

updates.summary: Preserve player-bound and graveyard-owner scopes on 'their', 'your', and 'each other player' references.
updates.evidence: Anya compares against each bound opponent's starting life total (Bound(0), not Acting); Endless Detour targets any 'card in a graveyard', not only AbilityController's graveyard; Rootcoil Creeper and Lord of the Forsaken restrict mana to spells cast 'from your graveyard' (One(AbilityController), not All); Underworld Cerberus and Grave Sifter return cards from each bound player's own graveyard (One(Bound(0)), not All); The Council of Four checks a player's second card 'during their turn' (One(Active), not All); Thoughtbound Primoc, Wild Mammoth, and Damping Engine compare against 'each other player' (OthersThan(Bound(0)), not All).

updates.summary: Preserve explicit chooser and controller clauses on library placement and battlefield entry.
updates.evidence: Hinder and Not Forgotten specify 'your choice of the top or bottom of its owner's library' (AbilityController chooses, not Owners); The Cyber-Controller puts milled creature cards onto the battlefield 'under your control' (Player(AbilityController), not Owner).

updates.summary: Countering 'all abilities' targets stack objects of kind Ability, not Spell.
updates.evidence: Summary Dismissal says 'counter all abilities' and Kadena's Silencer says 'counter all abilities your opponents control'; MTGish exported object kind Spell instead of Ability on both.

updates.summary: Preserve swapped or misbound object, attachment, and result references.
updates.evidence: Oko, the Trickster prevents damage dealt 'to him' (Source, not Target(0,0)); Ogre Geargrabber attaches Target(0,0) to Source (MTGish swapped attachments and host); Karona, False God Avatar exchanges Result(0,0) with Result(1,0) (MTGish referenced Result(0,1)); Keen Duelist loses life equal to the other player's revealed card (Recorded(0), not Recorded(1)); Three Tree Battalion perpetually modifies the conjured duplicate (result 3, not result 2); Flames of Moradin duplicates nontoken artifacts destroyed by result 0 (Matching(Transition(0, Before)), not all Battlefield artifacts); Technomancer chooses artifact creature cards 'from your graveyard' (Zone(Graveyard), not only the 3 milled cards in Recorded(0)).

updates.summary: Preserve comparison operators, aggregations, and boolean connectives (NotEqual, Less, Maximum, AnyOf, Not).
updates.evidence: Iridian Maelstrom checks 'isn't all colors' (NotEqual, not Equal); Skull Raid ('fewer than two') and Jackdaw Savior ('lesser mana value') test strict Less, not LessOrEqual; Timely Reinforcements ('fewer creatures than an opponent') compares against Maximum opponent creature count, not Minimum; Decree of Annihilation ('artifacts, creatures, and lands'), Squall ('power or toughness equal'), Mentor's Guidance ('planeswalker, Cleric, Druid, Shaman, Warlock, or Wizard'), and Slime Against Humanity ('Oozes or named Slime Against Humanity') are disjunctions (AnyOf), not conjunctions (AllOf); Katsumasa checks 'if it's not a Vehicle' (Not(Subtype(Vehicle)), not Subtype(Vehicle)).

updates.summary: Preserve explicit face-down visibility, secret choice, play-permission terms, choice costs, and optional wrappers.
updates.evidence: Expensive Taste exiles cards 'face down' (FaceDown, not FaceUp); Cunning Azurescale and Divining Dive 'secretly choose' (secret: true); Wheel of Misfortune restricts to '0 or greater' (options: [Comparison(GreaterOrEqual, 0)]); Whispersteel Dagger has no exile replacement (into_exile: false); Elder Brain lets you spend mana as any color at normal cost (cost: Normal, spend_as: AnyColor, not Free); Torment of Hailfire offers a Choice between sacrificing or discarding, not paying both; Hope-Ender Coatl counters 'unless they pay {1}' (If(Not(PaymentChosen(0)))), not unconditionally; Expedited Inheritance ('may exile') and Sheoldred's Assimilator ('you may conjure') are Optional.

updates.summary: Preserve explicit characteristic, subtype, and property checks (BasePower/BaseToughness, Toughness, Spacecraft, CreatureTypes, AddCardType(Creature)).
updates.evidence: Angelic Aberration checks 'base power or toughness 1 or less' (BasePower/BaseToughness); Evolving Adaptive compares toughness against this creature's Toughness, not Power; Network Marauder buffs 'Spacecraft cards', not Equipment; Menagerie Curator checks 'share a creature type' with a creature card in your library (SharesWithAny(CreatureTypes), not SharesNameWithAny); Waker of the Wilds animates target land into a '0/0 Elemental creature' (including AddCardType(Creature)).

updates.summary: Preserve explicit control, ownership, and CardType(Creature) filter conjuncts.
updates.evidence: Grand Ossuary ('creatures they control'), Mirror of the Forebears ('target creature you control'), Tamanoa and Disciples of the Inferno ('noncreature source you control'), Trial of Agony ('controlled by the same opponent'), Benevolent Blessing ('Auras and Equipment you control'), Shaun ('creature you control'), and Rift Elemental ('suspended card you own') omitted or inverted their controller/owner conjunct; Olag, Purging Scythe, High Score, Primal Empathy, and Éomer omitted CardType(Creature); Szat's Will omitted OpponentsOf scope and Creature card filter on exiled cards.

updates.summary: Preserve explicit zone, turn-window, event-subject, and self-exclusion constraints.
updates.evidence: Harsh Mentor triggers on abilities 'on the battlefield' (InZone(Battlefield)); Corpse Appraiser checks 'put into exile this way' (InZone(Exile)); Seshiro the Anointed Avatar excludes 'the battlefield or the stack' (adding Not(InZone(Stack))); Molten Lavamancer triggers 'during your turn' (Filtered(PlayerIsActive(AbilityController))); Ever-Watching Threshold tests 'if they attacked' (Attack.by: One(EventSubject)); Psychic Battle triggers on any player choosing targets without an unprinted Psychic Battle exclusion; Boltbender ('other spells or abilities'), Nicol Bolas, Dragon-God ('all other planeswalkers'), and Archfiend of Ifnir / Curator of Mysteries / Horror of the Broken Lands ('cycle or discard another card') require self-exclusion.

updates.summary: Restore omitted controller, zone, non-self, and target-kind filter predicates
updates.evidence: Oracle wording explicitly constrains controller ("you control", "they control", "opponents control"), zone ("from your graveyard", "from a graveyard", "other than the battlefield or the stack", "on the battlefield"), non-self ("another", "other"), or target kind ("permanent or player", "you or a permanent you control"), whereas MTGish gold dropped or inverted those filter terms.

updates.summary: Correct inverted AllOf/AnyOf connectives, erroneous Subtype(Saga), and bogus ColorCount filter
